name: Mao Zedong
role: Chinese Communist Party chairman (1943–1976) and leader of the People’s Republic of China
summary: Mao advocated Communist Party leadership, socialist public ownership, collective agriculture and continuing class struggle. His revolutionary mass campaigns sought to transform political authority and culture as well as economic production; his later diplomacy pursued cooperation against Soviet power.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He called for developing a powerful army, navy and air force.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He coupled socialist transformation with a technological revolution toward modern machine production.

bound-labor.rationale: His New Democracy programme confiscated landlord estates and ended feudal land relations.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He linked war’s historical origins to private property and classes and described the First World War as imperialist.

central-planning.rationale: He required cooperative production to follow unified state economic planning.

class-collaboration.rationale: His mature account retained class struggle between workers and capitalists under socialism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He described civilization’s history as classes struggling, triumphing and being eliminated.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: In 1975 he warned that bourgeois elements within the Party could re-establish capitalism.

collective-farming.rationale: He insisted agricultural collectivisation was necessary to consolidate socialism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His 1963 statement supported Black Americans’ struggle against racial discrimination.

death-penalty.rationale: He retained execution for grave counter-revolutionary crimes while urging restrictions and warning against irreversible mistakes.

decide-locally.rationale: He favoured greater local initiative alongside strengthened unified central leadership.

defeat-communism.rationale: He described communism as the ultimate goal of his political work.

democracy-best.rationale: He rejected abstract democracy and defended dictatorship against classes resisting socialism.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He rejected competitive two-party government as bourgeois dictatorship rather than a sufficient test of democracy.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He defended working-class-led dictatorship over exploiters and opponents of socialist transformation.

direct-action.rationale: He called armed seizure of political power the central task of revolution universally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He advocated women’s equal participation in productive and political activity.

dominated-front.rationale: He called for the broadest international front against imperialist aggression and control.

equal-outcomes.rationale: His 1975 remarks urged restricting unequal wage scales and bourgeois rights within socialism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He defended unity of China’s different nationalities and opposed Han chauvinism.

gradual-change.rationale: In his 1927 Hunan report he wrote 'a revolution is not a dinner party, or writing an essay, or painting a picture, or doing embroidery; it cannot be so refined, so leisurely and gentle, so temperate, kind, courteous, restrained and magnanimous. A revolution is an insurrection, an act of violence by which one class overthrows another'.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He said China needed atomic bombs to avoid being bullied by foreign powers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He presented modern socialist industry and agriculture as desirable goals.

informal-organisation.rationale: He insisted on a permanent disciplined revolutionary party to organise the masses.

land-redistribution.rationale: He explicitly proposed confiscating landlord land and distributing it to landless and land-poor peasants.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: His late remarks treated commodity exchange as a source of capitalist restoration to restrict under proletarian dictatorship.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He treated cultural production as class-bound and politically effective in sustaining or challenging social power.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He located social development in contradictions of productive forces, production relations and classes.

multipolar-world.rationale: His three-worlds strategy supported developing countries and intermediate powers resisting superpower domination.

nation-first.rationale: He opposed narrow nationalism and tied Chinese liberation to international working-class solidarity.

national-resource-control.rationale: He proposed state ownership of major banks and enterprises to prevent private domination of national livelihood.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He expressly championed communism as the most progressive social system.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He explicitly supported participation in just wars and armed resistance to aggression.

one-party-rule.rationale: He called the Communist Party the indispensable leadership core of socialist society.

party-commands-army.rationale: He explicitly required the Party to command the gun.

party-controls-media.rationale: He demanded that literature and art serve proletarian revolutionary politics, rather than political independence.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He identified political, familial, religious and husbandly authority as a system binding women.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He explicitly joined patriotic national liberation with the emancipation of workers.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He advocated a national culture while critically rejecting its feudal elements and absorbing useful foreign culture.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He demanded that poor and lower-middle peasants dominate cooperative leadership.

private-courts-defense.rationale: His army was a public revolutionary force under Communist Party leadership, rather than a commercial service.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He explicitly described capitalists’ profits from the working class as exploitation.

property-franchise.rationale: He demanded suffrage without property or education qualifications for the revolutionary people.

public-ownership.rationale: He explicitly advocated replacing private industry and commerce with socialist public ownership.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He advocated a scientific culture opposed to superstition, with truth tested in objective practice.

rehabilitation.rationale: He favoured reform through labour and giving captured counter-revolutionaries a chance to begin again.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: He listed religious authority among the principal systems oppressing Chinese women.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Sixteen Points adopted by the Central Committee on 8 August 1966 under his leadership said that the bourgeoisie 'is still trying to use the old ideas, culture, customs and habits of the exploiting classes to corrupt the masses' and that the proletariat must 'use the new ideas, culture, customs and habits of the proletariat to change the mental outlook of the whole of society'; the text calls for struggle against old culture's influence, not explicitly for its destruction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He said oppressed peoples must rely first on their own struggle and only second on international assistance.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He welcomed the weakening of husbands’ dominance and women gaining greater household decision-making power.

smash-state-machine.rationale: His universal prescription was to overthrow reactionary rule through armed seizure and create revolutionary political power.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He explained both socialist and bourgeois states as class dictatorships.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He discussed allocating state investment among heavy industry, agriculture, light industry and defence.

state-harmful.rationale: He defended revolutionary state power and maintained a permanent fighting force after victory.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: He called for strengthening state power while imperialism and domestic reaction remained.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: His later strategy opposed superpower hegemony but sought practical cooperation with the United States against the Soviet Union.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He endorsed arrest and deprivation of political rights for opponents classified as counter-revolutionaries.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He demanded complete rejection of great-power chauvinism, even after China became strong.

total-state.rationale: He treated culture and art as components of the revolutionary political project. His economic programme likewise subordinated production to socialism.

traditional-family.rationale: His criticism of feudal family authority and husbands’ dominance rejects the traditional patriarchal family as a social foundation.

vanguard-party.rationale: He said a disciplined Marxist-Leninist revolutionary party was necessary to lead workers to victory.

war-builds-character.rationale: He said just revolutionary war could purge weaknesses and transform both China and Japan.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He opposed the individual peasant economy and its tendency to produce rich peasants.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He explicitly said genuine sex equality required socialist transformation of society.

women-suffrage.rationale: He specified universal and equal suffrage irrespective of sex.

worker-ownership.rationale: His socialist transformation transferred production to public and cooperative ownership, rather than private employers.

workers-nation.rationale: He urged unity with workers across capitalist countries, including Japan and the United States.

workers-own-party.rationale: He advocated a revolutionary Communist Party leading the working class against imperialism.

notes:
The New Democracy programme describes a transitional stage; later collectivisation and the 1975 remarks govern mature economic answers. Cultural policy is assessed against the later record where it departed from the Hundred Flowers language. No modern digital or climate positions are assigned. The atomic-energy inference is distinguished from direct evidence for an independent bomb.

Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-14): brought to rules 7. The four Wikipedia-only answers were re-sourced (gradual-change to his 1927 Hunan report; sacrifice-heritage to the Sixteen Points) or nulled (return-to-foraging, leader-cult) after searching the Marxists Internet Archive texts (his works are not in the local marxists corpus).
